Resolves #21449

A header drop or a region change renumbers the grid's headers. It writes `aria-colindex` into each header's vdom and ships the writes with the toolbar's update at depth 2. When one header's own update merged into that cycle, the cycle was built sparse, and every other header kept its old index in the DOM. `grid.header.Toolbar#syncAriaColumnIndexes()` now owns the write, and it marks a changed cycle `denseUpdate`, so every header ships its new index. The drop, the Wrapper's re-sync and `createItems` call it, which replaces three inline loops.

Evidence: L3 (a unit red-first on the production re-sync path; a real-browser battery of the e2e release arm, outside CI) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-5). Residual: the 60-run CI watch in Post-Merge Validation.

Change class: restoration (`fix`). The method replaces three existing writers and adds no behavior. agent-preflight: not hosted here; the pre-commit and pre-push guards ran.

Prescription checked: `src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs` owns the concern. The toolbar owns header positions and `ariaColumnOffset`, and `denseUpdate` is the engine's documented contract for an owner's silent child writes (`VdomLifecycle.mjs:43-49`). Rejected:
- **Inferring dense from any owner-raised depth in `VdomLifecycle`.** #19404 declined this as an engine design change, and it would also make every structural move dense.
- **A reactive per-header index config.** It adds public surface for a value only the toolbar can compute.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/grid/AriaRegions.spec.mjs` "a header whose own update joins the renumbering leaves no other header on its old index". Red at `87e0ae1bc4`, where `name` shipped 3 and two headers read 3; green here |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/draggable/grid/header/toolbar/SortZone.spec.mjs` asserts that the drop calls `syncAriaColumnIndexes` before it measures. Red at `87e0ae1bc4` |
| AC-3 | `git grep -n "aria-colindex'\] =" -- src/grid/header src/draggable/grid/header` returns only the write inside `Toolbar#syncAriaColumnIndexes` |
| AC-4 | Outside CI: the release arm, 25 runs on efficiency cores, with 0 stalls here versus 1 at `87e0ae1bc4`. The full `HeaderGroups.spec.mjs` + `HeaderGroupsTheme.spec.mjs` pass 28 of 28 here (Test Evidence). Both also run in CI's e2e-engine |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: the unit suite. Locally: 8098 passed, 2 skipped |

## Deltas from ticket
None substantive. `Toolbar#afterSetSortable` is the same class in a touched file: out of scope, noted in #21451, where it is measured red.

## Test Evidence
- **The sighting at `87e0ae1bc4`.** The release arm stalled in 1 of 25 runs with the whole browser on efficiency cores (`taskpolicy -c background`, 2× page throttling). Main-thread CPU throttling alone gave 0 stalls in 32 runs at 4× and 8×, because the race lives in worker timing. At the stall no header was missing. The moved headers kept their old index:

  | Header | Jul | Aug | Sep | Apr | May | Jun |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | position | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 |
  | `aria-colindex` in the DOM | 8 | 9 | 10 | 8 | 9 | 10 |

- **This head.** The same 25-run battery, with the same probe and flags, ran 25 of 25 with no stall. A 1-in-25 sighting is too rare for a 25-run battery to prove the fix. The unit red-first below is the proof; the battery shows the arm holds.
- **Red-first.** The two touched specs fail 2 of 21 at `87e0ae1bc4` (the new AC-1 test and AC-2's call order) and pass 21 of 21 here.
- **Header moves end to end.** Eight other grid specs that move headers or change their regions pass 20 of 20 here: `ColumnCrossBodyDnD`, `ColumnOverdragScroll`, `LockedDnDDuplication`, `LockedRegionEmpties`, `HeaderCellRectSync`, `HeaderResizeRectSync`, `PinnedColumnsExample` and `LockedCellHorizontalStability`.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] No `HeaderGroups.spec.mjs:810` "still off" failure in the next 60 engine e2e runs.
